text:
kevin: weird onefirst call from our multi-tenant test harness returns 403 billing: workspace_unprovisioned even though the org is provisioned. The token looks fine but it has `tid` set to the customer's tenant and aud is our client id. anyone seen tenant claim mismatches?

kevin: logs:```
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z auth: token validated aud=api.redwood.ai client_id=cli-xyz tid=tenant:acme-corp sub=service-account-123
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z provision: org_lookup failed for tid=tenant:acme-corp, fallback tried email mapping -> none
2026-04-04T09:12:01Z caller=client.go status=403 msg=\"billing: workspace_unprovisioned\"
```

tara: the provisioning logic tries tenant->org binding then email->org. If tid is present but not bound to an org we fall back to email. Multi-tenant service accounts often have tid but no org binding so provisioning fails.

julio: short term workaround: include header `x-redwood-org` or use an org-scoped token. Example that worked for kevin:```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"x-redwood-org: org_0AX1B2\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-mini","input":"hi"}'
```

kevin: adding header fixed it and I got a 200 + stream start. but this caught a bunch of customers doing multi-tenant integrations. we should make onboarding clearer.

tara: filing INF-5132: "multi-tenant tokens: improve tenant->org mapping and doc quick fixes". will add: 1) diagnostic endpoint in quickstart that echoes detected claims (aud, azp, tid, email); 2) quickstart env REDWOOD_ORG support so sample containers set header; 3) clearer error code `missing_org_binding` instead of generic `workspace_unprovisioned`.

julio: SDK parity: node currently surfaces 403 with string message, python returns structured json code. team should converge on `missing_org_binding` across SDKs. filing INF-5133.

devex-bot: deploy: payg-provisioning-guard v1.3.6 rolled out 2026-04-04T08:30:00Z  tightened tenant->org checks.

kevin: thanks all. temporary note for customers: if you use multi-tenant or third-party service accounts, set x-redwood-org on the request or use an org-scoped token. i'll PR a short snippet into the multi-tenant quickstart README. :thumbsup:
